Going into the second lap the Thames man, now identified as 2nd-claimer Larry Matthews from Salford, made his break and forced open what began to look like a winning lead.

Through the woods and then climbing back up to the end of the first lap it was Munt (Herne Hill), Matthews (Thames H&H), Major (South London), Marriott (Hercules Wimbledon) and Lee Hurst bowling along at the front with barely a whisker between them.
Fastest: L.Matthews (TH&H n/s) 13:44; A.Stewart (Belgrave) 14:02; G.Staines (SLH) 14:08; P.Haywood (Boxhill) 14:10; A.Moses (Reigate) 14:11; J.Simpson (SLH) 14:12.
Paul Freary now took the opportunity to move our colours into a half minute lead as an unfit Larry Matthews slipped back down the field for Thames and Bedford consolidated their second place.
